goal: As Haven & Hearth's online store manager, produce four linked deliverables: a Word complaint-response package with an internal Triage Note per ticket (catalog cross-check, margin context, action); an Excel dashboard with Profit Margin Analysis, Traffic-to-Sales Funnel and Underperformer Crosswalk sheets; a 2-3 page PDF sentiment audit of the reviews dataset that cross-checks listing copy against complaint themes; and optimized_product_listings.csv with justified rewrites.
delivered: complaint_triage_response_package.docx (responses + triage notes for all open tickets), integrated_performance_dashboard.xlsx (three correctly named sheets), customer_sentiment_catalog_alignment_audit.pdf (3 pages; Trend/Dresses/Blouses correctly chosen with the >=30-review rule) and optimized_product_listings.csv with rewrites and a justification column.
what_went_wrong: Customer responses applied the policies in substance but never named the policy sections (Shipping Policy, Return & Exchange Policy, Product Quality Guarantee, etc.) and dropped some terms (original shipping refund, 60-day defective window). The PDF cross-check stayed at category level, quoting no listing phrase against review phrases and never flagging the Yellow Wool Jumper 'soft wool blend' copy; this one gap cost both R2 and R5. Every triage note used the same 12.47% portfolio margin line and made no per-product category mapping or margin-driven recommendation.

failed_items.why: store_policies.docx names each section (1. Shipping Policy, 2. Return & Exchange Policy, 3. Pricing & Promotions Policy, 6. Product Quality Guarantee) and the agent read it, but the responses only say 'under our guarantee' (docx line 36). The 7-day rule appears only in an internal note, and the original-shipping refund and 60- vs 30-day window are omitted.

The audit maps class themes to generic catalog gaps ('no measurements', avoid 'premium'/'perfect') and never quotes listing text against review text. The Yellow Wool-Blend Jumper appears only as a fit recommendation (PDF line 130), with no wool-quality contradiction. The inputs had both listings and reviews; Sweaters is outside the agent's three selected classes, which partly explains that miss.

PDF format, length and sections 1, 2 and 4 passed. The criterion fails on the same Section 3 weakness as R2: no SKU- or class-level listing-vs-review language comparison, and the PDF itself says review SKUs cannot be mapped to store products.

Each triage note ends with the identical 'Portfolio proxy is 12.47% overall margin; use it for prioritization, not item economics' (e.g. docx lines 57, 69). It gives no category/sub-category lookup or directional proxy (Leather Tote as high-price item, Clay Plant Pot as home goods), and margin never drives the retain/remove call. The domain mismatch was correctly acknowledged.
